review_evidence: Focused schema, runtime hash, pedagogy, freshness, coverage, and key self-review for eng_c4_ch07 on 2026-07-12
title: Fit Body, Fit Mind, Fit Nation
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Find the message in an active routine
levels.focus: identify a paragraph main idea from several healthy habits
levels.teaching_goal: Connect movement, rest, food, and regular practice to a balanced idea about fitness.

guided_check.teaching_block: A paragraph's main idea must fit all key details. Worked example: skipping builds movement, water replaces fluid, and sleep restores energy. The broad idea is that fitness depends on a balanced routine, not on one hard exercise.
guided_check.passage: Before school, Dev skips for ten minutes. He carries water, eats a fresh breakfast, and goes to bed at a regular time. He feels ready for class and games.
guided_check.prompt: Which statement gives the whole paragraph's main idea?
options: several regular habits support fitness and energy
skipping is the only useful exercise
breakfast should be eaten at night
accepted_answers: several regular habits support fitness and energy

bridge.teaching_block: Group the details: cycling and stretching are movement; water and rest support recovery. Then choose an idea that includes both groups.
bridge.passage: Lata cycles in the park, stretches after the ride, drinks water, and rests before homework.
options: they form a balanced fitness routine
accepted_answers: they form a balanced fitness routine

masterclass.teaching_block: Misconception check: a catchy detail is not always the main idea. If a paragraph includes exercise, rest, and steady practice, an answer only about winning a race is too narrow.
masterclass.passage: The relay team practises short runs three days a week. On other days, members walk, stretch, and rest tired muscles. Their coach praises steady improvement rather than only first place.
masterclass.prompt: Which idea best covers the paragraph?
options: regular practice and recovery matter more than only winning
relay runners must train every hour
first place is the coach's only goal
accepted_answers: regular practice and recovery matter more than only winning
steady practice and rest build fitness

independent_check.teaching_block: Read the unseen paragraph and state the main idea in your own words without choices.
independent_check.passage: Each afternoon, the children choose a different activity: kho-kho on Monday, dance on Tuesday, and yoga on Wednesday. They warm up first and cool down afterwards. No one is forced to move beyond a safe limit.
independent_check.prompt: What is the main idea of this paragraph?

concept_slots.description: Recognises regular or varied physical activity.
Includes safe limits, warming up, or cooling down.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer main-idea reading to a study routine. Combine work habits and recovery into one broad statement.
transfer_check.passage: Before a mathematics test, Ina studies in twenty-minute blocks. Between blocks she stands, stretches, and looks away from the screen. She stops early enough to sleep well.
transfer_check.prompt: State the paragraph's main idea in your own words.

concept_slots.description: Mentions planned or focused study periods.
Connects breaks, movement, or sleep to effective preparation.

levels.title: Explain how movement supports body and mind
levels.focus: infer a benefit and support it with a passage clue
levels.teaching_goal: Use an observed change as evidence when explaining why a healthy choice helps.

guided_check.teaching_block: A reason needs evidence. Worked example: 'The walk helped Riya concentrate because she returned calmer and completed her work without leaving her seat.' The result supports the claim.
guided_check.passage: After sitting over a puzzle for a long time, Kabir took a brisk walk. He returned, noticed a missed clue, and solved the puzzle calmly.
guided_check.prompt: Why can the walk be said to help Kabir's mind?
options: he returns calm and notices a clue
walking gives him the answer directly
accepted_answers: he returns calm and notices a clue

bridge.teaching_block: Build the explanation in two steps: action, then observed result. Action: practise balance. Result: steadier movement on uneven ground.
bridge.passage: Nima practised standing on one foot each morning. After a week, she crossed the stepping stones with fewer wobbles.
bridge.prompt: Which result is evidence that practice helped?

masterclass.teaching_block: Misconception check: 'exercise is good' is a claim, not evidence. Point to a measurable or visible change in the passage.
masterclass.passage: At first, Omar paused twice while climbing the school stairs. After a month of regular swimming, he reached the top without stopping and could still speak comfortably.
masterclass.prompt: Which detail best supports improved stamina?
options: he reaches the top without stopping
accepted_answers: he reaches the top without stopping

independent_check.teaching_block: Explain the benefit in this unseen scene using a precise clue. Do not rely on a general slogan.
independent_check.passage: Mira felt restless after an hour of reading. She joined a five-minute rhythm exercise, returned to her desk, and wrote the next paragraph without tapping or looking around.
independent_check.prompt: How did the movement break help Mira? Use evidence.

concept_slots.description: Explains improved calm, focus, or readiness to work.
Uses the completed paragraph or stopped tapping and looking around as evidence.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply action-result reasoning to a community habit rather than a school exercise.
transfer_check.passage: Residents began walking to nearby shops on weekend mornings. After six weeks, they reported less breathlessness on the hill and talked with neighbours more often.
transfer_check.prompt: Give two evidence-backed reasons the walking habit was useful.
transfer_check.preflight_rule: The response must give two distinct English reasons and link each to evidence in the passage.

rubric_criteria.description: Explains the fitness benefit using reduced breathlessness on the hill.
Explains the community benefit using more neighbour conversations.
Clearly connects each claimed benefit to the observed result.

levels.title: Use fitness words from context
levels.focus: infer precise meanings from actions and results
levels.teaching_goal: Use context to understand stamina, balance, flexible, pulse, and recover.

guided_check.teaching_block: Context often shows a word through a result. Worked example: if a cyclist can continue for a long distance without tiring, stamina means the ability to keep doing an activity.
guided_check.passage: Aarav built stamina by cycling a little farther each week until he could ride for forty minutes without stopping.

bridge.teaching_block: Use the action clue. If someone stays steady and does not tip, the word is balance.
bridge.passage: Leena held her balance on the low beam, keeping her body steady from one end to the other.

masterclass.teaching_block: Misconception check: flexible can describe a body that bends easily or a plan that can change. Test the meaning against the surrounding sentence.
masterclass.passage: After gentle stretching, her shoulders felt flexible and moved through a wider range without strain.
masterclass.prompt: What does flexible mean in this fitness context?
options: able to bend or move easily
accepted_answers: able to bend or move easily

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the unseen sentence clue to explain the word.
independent_check.passage: After the sprint, Jay placed two fingers on his wrist and counted his pulse, the repeated beat caused by his heart pumping blood.
accepted_answers: the beat caused by the heart

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer the word recover to a music rehearsal. Use the rest-and-return clue.
transfer_check.passage: After singing the difficult section, the choir paused to recover. A few minutes later, their breathing was calm and they began again.
transfer_check.prompt: What does recover mean in this context?

levels.title: Describe routines in the right tense
levels.focus: use adjectives and present or past tense according to context
levels.teaching_goal: Choose precise adjectives and match verb tense to regular habits or completed past actions.

guided_check.teaching_block: An adjective describes a noun; tense locates an action in time. In 'The steady runner practises daily', steady describes runner and practises shows a regular habit.
guided_check.passage: The agile goalkeeper moves quickly from one side of the goal to the other every evening.

bridge.teaching_block: Look for the time marker. Every morning signals a routine, so use the simple present. Yesterday signals a completed past action.
bridge.passage: Every morning, Pia ___ her ankles before she runs.
bridge.prompt: Which verb fits a regular habit?

masterclass.teaching_block: Misconception check: an -ed form does not fit every sentence about exercise. Match the verb to the time clue, not to the topic.
masterclass.passage: Last Saturday, the team ___ a five-kilometre charity walk.
masterclass.prompt: Which verb correctly shows a finished past action?

independent_check.teaching_block: Use the time clue to write the correct verb without choices.
independent_check.passage: On school days, Rohan ___ two rounds of the field before assembly. Verb: walk.
independent_check.prompt: Which present-tense form completes Rohan's school-day routine?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer tense choice to a completed gardening action.
transfer_check.passage: Yesterday, the neighbours ___ ten saplings along the lane. Verb: plant.
transfer_check.prompt: Which past-tense form completes the sentence about yesterday's planting?

levels.title: Summarise and write a balanced activity plan
levels.focus: select key advice and produce a clear plan in one's own words
levels.teaching_goal: Turn several fitness details into a concise summary and a realistic sequence of complete sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: A summary keeps the central advice, not every example. Worked example: walking, dance, and games are different activities; warm-up and rest are safety habits. A concise summary is 'Choose enjoyable movement regularly and allow the body to prepare and recover.'
guided_check.passage: The coach suggests brisk walking, folk dance, or a ball game for movement. She also asks children to warm up, drink water, and rest when pain begins.
guided_check.prompt: Which sentence best summarises the advice?
options: Move regularly in an enjoyable way and follow safe habits.
Only ball games count as movement.
Every child must choose the same activity.
accepted_answers: Move regularly in an enjoyable way and follow safe habits.

bridge.teaching_block: Plan before writing: choose one movement action, one safety action, and one recovery action. Turn each into a complete sentence with a subject and verb.
bridge.passage: Plan notes: Tuesday - cycle 20 minutes; before - warm up; after - drink water and rest.
bridge.prompt: Which opening sentence is complete and follows the plan?
options: On Tuesday, I will cycle for twenty minutes.
accepted_answers: On Tuesday, I will cycle for twenty minutes.

masterclass.teaching_block: Misconception check: a harder plan is not automatically a better plan. A useful plan is specific, balanced, safe, and possible to repeat.
masterclass.passage: Plan A: sprint for two hours every day without rest. Plan B: walk or play for twenty minutes on four days, warm up first, and rest if pain begins.
masterclass.prompt: Which plan is more balanced and sustainable?

independent_check.teaching_block: Write an original three-sentence plan from the unseen notes. Include movement, safety, and recovery without copying the note fragments.
independent_check.passage: Thursday notes: playground badminton / five-minute warm-up / water break after the game.
independent_check.prompt: Write a clear three-sentence activity plan in your own words.
independent_check.preflight_rule: The response must contain complete English sentences that turn all three notes into a realistic Thursday activity plan.

rubric_criteria.description: Plans badminton or equivalent play on Thursday.
Includes a five-minute warm-up before play.
Includes a water break after the game.
Uses clear, complete sentences and original wording.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer balanced planning to a school event. Summarise the work-and-rest schedule in complete sentences.
transfer_check.passage: Clean-up day notes: sweep one classroom / pause and wash hands / sort paper for recycling / finish before lunch.
transfer_check.prompt: Write a short, ordered plan in your own words.
transfer_check.preflight_rule: The response must present the clean-up actions in a sensible order using complete English sentences and include the hygiene break.

rubric_criteria.description: Begins with or clearly includes sweeping one classroom.
Includes sorting paper for recycling before lunch.
Uses an understandable sequence of complete sentences in original wording.

items.passage: The class begins games period with gentle stretches, plays in small groups, drinks water, and ends with slow breathing. The routine helps everyone move safely from start to finish.
items.prompt: Which main idea covers all the details?
options: a complete activity routine includes preparation play and recovery
slow breathing is the only exercise
water should be saved until bedtime
small groups never need safety rules
accepted_answers: a complete activity routine includes preparation play and recovery

items.passage: Sana alternates active days with easier days. She jogs on Monday, walks on Tuesday, practises dance on Wednesday, and sleeps at a regular time. Her energy remains steady through the week.
items.prompt: State the main idea in your own words.

concept_slots.description: Mentions varied or regular activity across the week.
Connects rest or steady sleep to maintaining energy.

items.passage: The group warms up, completes two relay rounds, and then walks slowly until breathing returns to normal.
items.prompt: What does the group do after the relay rounds?

items.passage: Vikram packs a banana and water before practice. At the field, he eats the banana first and saves the water for breaks.
items.prompt: What does Vikram save for breaks?

items.passage: After daily throwing practice, Neha's passes land closer to her partner and fewer balls roll away.
items.prompt: Which evidence shows that practice improved her control?
options: her passes land closer and fewer balls roll away
accepted_answers: her passes land closer and fewer balls roll away

items.passage: Before the breathing exercise, Ali rushed through his reading. Afterwards, he read the next page at an even pace and corrected a missed word himself.
items.prompt: Explain how the exercise may have helped, using evidence.

concept_slots.description: Infers improved calm, focus, or control.
Uses even pace or self-correction as evidence.

items.passage: The children moved the practice cones farther apart only after everyone could turn safely at the first distance.
items.prompt: Why did they wait before increasing the distance?
options: to build difficulty after mastering safe turns
accepted_answers: to build difficulty after mastering safe turns
everyone needed to turn safely first

items.passage: It was very hot, so the coach shortened each running round and added more water breaks under shade.
items.prompt: Write an evidence-backed reason for changing the practice.

concept_slots.description: Mentions the heat or hot weather.
Explains that shorter rounds and water or shade reduce risk and keep players safe.

items.passage: The hikers built endurance until they could walk the full trail without an extra stop.
items.prompt: Which chapter word means endurance?

items.passage: After the race, the runner rested until her breathing returned to normal and her strength came back.
items.prompt: Write the chapter word for resting and regaining strength.

items.passage: The gymnast remained stable on the narrow platform even when she lifted one foot.
items.prompt: What does stable suggest about her balance?

items.passage: The flexible branch bent in the wind and returned to its shape instead of snapping.
items.prompt: What does flexible mean here?

items.passage: The energetic dancers completed the final routine with wide smiles.
items.prompt: Which adjective describes the dancers?

items.passage: Noun: swimmer. Details: calm, skilled. Action: crosses the pool with even strokes.
items.prompt: Write a complete sentence using the noun and at least one adjective.

concept_slots.description: States that the swimmer crosses the pool with even strokes.

items.passage: Every Sunday, the family ___ along the river path. Verb: cycle.
items.prompt: Choose the correct verb for a regular habit.

items.passage: Last evening, the players ___ their new passing drill. Verb: practise.
items.prompt: Write the correct past-tense verb.

items.passage: A coach advises children to move on most days, choose activities they enjoy, begin gently, and stop when sharp pain appears.
items.prompt: Which summary keeps the coach's central message about regular and safe movement?
options: Exercise regularly in an enjoyable and safe way.
Sharp pain proves an activity is working.
Only one kind of movement is useful.
Children should always begin at full speed.
accepted_answers: Exercise regularly in an enjoyable and safe way.

items.passage: The school opens its field before class for walking, skipping, or quiet stretching. Students choose one activity, warm up, and finish in time for breakfast.
items.prompt: Summarise the routine in your own words.

concept_slots.description: Mentions choosing an activity before class.
Includes warming up and finishing before breakfast or class.

items.passage: Plan: Saturday morning / ten-minute walk / gentle stretches afterwards / water before returning home.
items.prompt: Which is a complete plan sentence?
options: On Saturday morning, I will walk for ten minutes.
accepted_answers: On Saturday morning, I will walk for ten minutes.

items.passage: Wednesday notes: play catch for fifteen minutes / keep a safe distance / cool down with slow walking.
items.prompt: Write two complete sentences that turn all the notes into a plan.
items.preflight_rule: The response must use complete English sentences and include the activity, safe distance, and cool-down from the notes.

rubric_criteria.description: Plans fifteen minutes of catch on Wednesday.
Includes slow walking as a cool-down.
Uses at least two clear complete sentences.
